source_text:
Ἀλλ' ἐξείλκυσεν ἡμᾶς
λόγος εἰς μῆκος λόγου. καὶ ἴσως γεγόναμεν ἐμπόδιον πατρικῆς διδασκαλίας.
orientation: Cyril pauses after a long chain of exhortations to acknowledge that his discourse has run long and may have delayed the father's teaching.
pass_a_gloss: But the word dragged us out into length of word. And perhaps we have become a hindrance to the fatherly teaching.

choices.term: ἐξείλκυσεν ἡμᾶς λόγος εἰς μῆκος λόγου
choices.english: the word dragged us out into length of word
choices.why: Keeps the wordplay of λόγος repeated as subject and object, and the literal force of ἐξέλκω as dragging out.
rejected: our discourse has run on at length
the argument has carried us far

choices.english: a hindrance to the fatherly teaching
choices.why: Literal rendering of the genitive as the thing hindered; 'fatherly' preserves the adjective's reference to the father's instruction.
rejected: an obstacle to the paternal instruction
in the way of the father's teaching

pass_b_english: But our discourse has stretched on at length. And perhaps we have become a hindrance to the fatherly teaching.

problems.quote: dragged us out into length of word
problems.why: Awkward calque; 'length of word' is not English idiom.
problems.fix: 'drawn us out to a lengthy discourse' (as in u02-open) or 'led us into wordiness.'

edits.old: dragged us out into length of word
edits.new: drawn us out to a lengthy discourse

fixed: The English 'dragged us out into length of word' is an awkward calque of ἐξείλκυσεν ἡμᾶς λόγος εἰς μῆκος λόγου; 'length of word' is not idiomatic English. Replaced with 'drawn us out to a lengthy discourse', which matches the source sense and the parallel phrasing in u02-open.

polish.changed: Rendered the Greek idiom for a lengthy speech into natural English and clarified that 'we' refers to the speaker's own discourse.

notes.quote: dragged us out into length of word
notes.why: Awkward calque; 'length of word' is not English idiom.
notes.fix: 'drawn us out to a lengthy discourse' (as in u02-open) or 'led us into wordiness.'
